name: Consensus Substituted for Evidence
description: Uses agreement among people or institutions as proof of truth, rather than presenting the underlying evidence.

name: Authoritative Claim Without Citation
description: Presents a claim as established on the authority of studies, research, data, science, experts or tradition, with no citation a reader can check. Naming who made a study is not a citation.

name: Dissent Dismissed by Label
description: Opposing viewpoints are dismissed through labeling rather than substantive rebuttal. The label substitutes for argument. Dismissal words that can be aimed at anyone ('cranks', 'shills', 'extremists') count wherever they appear; role words ('radicals', 'fanatics', 'bosses') count where the text applies them as a label ('they're just radicals'); a claim label ('misinformation') counts when it ends the phrase; and open frames count with any word in the slot ('only a ___ would say that', 'of course the ___ would say that', 'Typical ___!', 'Ignore the ___.'). The rule lists no group's name.

name: False Binary / False Dilemma
description: Frames a situation as having only two options ('either ... or', 'there is no middle ground', 'if you're not ..., you're ...'), leaving out any others.

name: Fear-Based Urgency
description: Uses catastrophic language or time pressure ('act now', 'too late', 'irreversible') alongside a call to act.

name: Shame or Social Pressure Language
description: Appeals to shame, guilt or what reasonable people supposedly think, in place of evidence or argument.

name: Emotional Appeal in Place of Argument
description: Uses emotionally charged phrasing where an argument or evidence would go.
